terms.definition: Correspondence between the text, intended meaning, and supportable world or source state.
The sequence that takes a reader from understanding to the intended next action.
A clause pattern in which the grammatical subject normally represents the actor or experiencer.
All rule-and-context combinations the system can evaluate, not necessarily generate.
The expression to which a later pronoun or reference expression points.
A proposition offered as true, probable, valuable, causal, definitional, predictive, or advisable.
A unit organized around a predicate and its participants or circumstances.
Surface links such as reference, repetition, substitution, conjunction, and lexical relation.
The reader-recoverable conceptual and rhetorical unity of a text.
A circumstance that must hold for a rule, claim, or action to apply.
A rule that normally improves the target genre or audience but may yield to a documented reason.
Persuasive writing designed to influence a defined decision or action.
A controlled alternative offered for rhetorical effect rather than enforced.
A grammatical or content-system relation in which one element relies on another.
The logical or rhetorical connection between propositions or passages.
Information used to support, test, bound, or challenge a claim.
The support obligation created by a specific or consequential claim.
A recurring communication form with characteristic reader expectations and moves.
Information the reader can already identify from context or shared knowledge.
A requirement that must pass or block publication or action.
A useful diagnostic or ranking rule that does not guarantee an outcome.
A structured topic such as concept, task, reference, or troubleshooting.
A multidimensional diagnostic and transformation grid for decomposing, varying, selecting, routing, and reviewing interventions.
The scale at which a writing object exists, from signal to content system.
The conceptual, relational, pragmatic, and emotional content a reader recovers.
Continuity between a source message and the destination it leads to.
Two examples differing in one controlled feature so its effect can be evaluated.
A noun form that represents an action, process, or quality.
The intended change in what a reader knows, feels, decides, or does.
The main rhetorical job performed by a paragraph.
A clause pattern that promotes the receiver or result while demoting or omitting the actor.
Communication designed so intended readers can find, understand, and use what they need.
The central expression of an event, action, process, relation, or state.
The degree to which a local issue or change affects dependent units.
The author, audience, purpose, text, and setting that constrain communication.
The enforcement class: hard constraint, context default, heuristic, or creative option.
The amount of text or system affected by an issue or intervention.
The least invasive change that fully resolves the diagnosed failure without creating a larger one.
Meaning carried indirectly beneath a character’s or speaker’s literal words.
The structural relations and order by which words and phrases form clauses and sentences.
The degree to which a reader completes the intended action correctly and safely.
A local adaptation of voice to subject, reader state, and moment.
The conditions under which a proposition would be true or false.
The degree to which readers can find, understand, and use the content.
The stable relationship and character projected by a text.
A grammar system that evaluates language across interacting linguistic, rhetorical, contextual, dynamic, and outcome dimensions.
The reasoning that connects evidence to a claim.
